title: Work order and part sale status labels read as before
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, in Review, billable.
  • Have a new part sale for this test for customer A, open.
  • Have a second browser window signed in as an Admin to the production test account (app.shopview.com), where Internal Work Orders is not released yet, so today's screen can be compared.
  • In that production window, have a new open part sale for this test, part sale P.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the part sale.
  3. Open part sale P in the production window.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The header status reads Review.

Step 2:

  • The part sale header shows its status with no Closed, Internal or No Charge label; note the status.

Step 3:

  • Part sale P's header shows the same status label as the part sale in step 2.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close), story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order)

  • Terminology: “Statuses are named as the app names them: Estimate, Approved, In Progress, Review, Complete, Invoiced, Paid and Declined. This feature adds the label Closed, which only the internal invoice carries underneath (Key Decisions); Authorization is a line status, not a work order status.”
  • Feature Overview, Out of Scope: “Part sales. A part sale to an internal customer is a regular billable part sale: no badge, no Convert action, no Close, no NO CHARGE stamp. Components shared with part sales change only for work orders.”
